prompt: Stage 2-1 augment round, 100 HP, level 4 with 10 gold. Your opener is four unpaired 1-costs and one tank component; the two strongest boards in the lobby already have 2-stars with an item. Stage 2 losses cost 2 to 4 HP, stage 3 losses 8 to 10, and the curve turns at 3-5. Which plan do you commit to?

lobby.note: 2-star 1-cost carry with a completed item, three units of one trait

options.label: Take the loss streak: buy pairs only, bank to 50 by 3-1, keep losing through 3-2, and convert at 3-5 with level 7 and a rolldown
Fight for the win streak: roll the 10 gold for pairs now, since a win streak pays the same
Loss-streak with no fixed round: keep banking until HP reaches 40, then roll
Loss-streak to 4-2 for the maximum streak gold and a level-8 rolldown

explanation:
You are not choosing whether to lose stage 2; the two boards with itemised 2-stars decided that; you are choosing whether to be paid for it. From 2-1 to 3-3 is eight fights; the streak gold climbs from 1 to 3 across them and adds about 15 gold on top of interest, which is why you reach 50 around 3-1 instead of 3-5. The HP bill is five stage 2 losses at 3 and three stage 3 losses at 9, roughly 42, so you reach 3-5 near 58 HP with 60 or more gold.

The exit is a round, not an HP number. At 3-5 a loss starts costing 12 to 15 and the streak still pays 3, so from there every loss is a bad trade. Streaking to 4-2 adds three losses at that price, about 35 HP, and you convert near 25 HP. Waiting for 40 HP triggers around 4-1, after the curve turned: the same mistake on a different clock.

Rolling 10 gold at 2-1 for pairs is losing the same fights with no interest.
principle: A loss streak is an income line with an exit round chosen at the start: convert at 3-5, before the damage curve makes losses expensive.
commonMistake: Loss-streaking with no exit round and converting at 4-2 from 25 HP, which is losing with extra steps.
hint: Add up the streak gold and the HP over the rounds until 3-5, then do the same sum for the rounds until 4-2.
